subject: The lathe itself, assembled in hidden-line isometric: plinth, platter and lacquer, the rail behind and the cutter head hanging over the disc on its arm.
controls: cut: scale - the swarf thread coiling from the stylus up to the suction tube grows from ~0.7x to 2x (node 2).
groove: position - the carriage, arm and head slide along the rail from the rim toward the spindle (~34 px on screen) and the cut band of turns widens behind it.
wear: count - dust specks settle on the lacquer, 0 to 14; none at 0.
rumble: rotation - the lacquer's top outline turns in plane about the spindle, up to ~30 deg, so the disc reads as wobbling on a worn bearing; still at 0.
risks: Stretch, and it mostly doesn't fit: P11 works because the instrument's parts are what the note selects (theseus' tiers); here no note selects anything and an effect gets no note input, so the 'stack' is just a portrait of the machine. The exception case is recognition: a lathe reads as a turntable at a glance, so the player knows which part is the head, the disc and the plinth without a legend. Against it: the drawing is about the machine, not the sound; cut's swarf coil is tiny at rest (under ~10 px) and hard to see; rumble's in-plane rotation of an ellipse is a fake tilt that may look like the disc sliding off the platter, and 30 deg is a lot; risk of reading as a stock-style product drawing next to TE's own objects.
